dialogue.content: 本日はロープレ宜しくお願い致します。時間になったら始めさせていただきます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for participating in the role-play today. We will begin when it is time.

dialogue.content: おはようございます。どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Good morning. Thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: (もし扱ってみたい事があれば遠慮なくおっしゃっていただけるとこちらもありがたいです、どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。)
dialogue.English: (If there's anything you'd like to work on, please don't hesitate to let me know; that would be helpful for me as well. Thank you.)

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます！どんなケースでも頑張りたいので宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you! I'll do my best with any case, so I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日はお越しいただきありがとうございます。初めにあなたの年齢と性別を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: おはようございます。はい、17歳女性です
dialogue.English: Good morning. Yes, I'm a 17-year-old female.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。本日はどのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: おとうさんがうざいんです
dialogue.English: My dad is so annoying.

dialogue.content: ええ、そうなんですね。もう少しどのような状況か教えてもらえますか？
dialogue.English: I see. Could you tell me a bit more about the situation?

dialogue.content: 門限とかうるさいし、なんか監視されてる感じっていうか、まじうざい
dialogue.English: He's strict about my curfew, and it feels like I'm being watched or something. It's seriously annoying.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええそうなんですね。監視されていて管理されているような気持ちになるんですね
dialogue.English: I understand. It sounds like you feel watched and controlled.

dialogue.content: それは、うっとうしくもなりますよね
dialogue.English: That must be very frustrating.

dialogue.content: まじでうざいですよ
dialogue.English: It's seriously so annoying.

dialogue.content: もう嫌で嫌で仕方がない
dialogue.English: I just hate it so much; I can't stand it.

dialogue.content: うんうん、嫌になってしまうのも自然な事かと思いますよ
dialogue.English: Mmm, I think it's natural to feel that way.

dialogue.content: お父さんのどんなところが一番いやになってしまいますか？
dialogue.English: What about your dad bothers you the most?

dialogue.content: え、そうなんですか？友達のお父さんとか仲いいし、うちは怒鳴ってばっか
dialogue.English: Oh, really? My friends get along with their dads, but mine just yells all the time.

dialogue.content: いちいち見てくるところとかほんと無理
dialogue.English: I really can't stand how he's always watching everything I do.

dialogue.content: ええ、そうなんですねお友達のお父さんと比べてしまうこともあるんですね余計嫌なところが際立ってしまいますよね
dialogue.English: I see. So you find yourself comparing him to your friends' fathers, and that makes the things you dislike stand out even more.

dialogue.content: そうか、そうか見てくるっていうのは、どんなことを見てくるんでしょう？
dialogue.English: I see, I see. When you say he "watches" you, what kinds of things is he watching?

dialogue.content: なんかみてくる
dialogue.English: He just... watches me.

dialogue.content: うざすぎ
dialogue.English: It's way too annoying.

dialogue.content: なるほど確かにいちいち見ないでよ！って感情が湧いてきてしまいますよね
dialogue.English: I understand. It makes sense that you'd feel like, "Quit watching me all the time!"

dialogue.content: そうなんです！！！！
dialogue.English: Exactly!!!!

dialogue.content: うちの親ってちょっとほかの家と違うんじゃないかって思う
dialogue.English: I feel like my parents might be a little different from other families.

dialogue.content: うん、うんそう思ってしまうんですよね
dialogue.English: Mmm, yes, you feel that way, don't you?

dialogue.content: 他の家庭と違うなって思ったのは、どんなところですか？
dialogue.English: What makes you feel that your family is different from others?

dialogue.content: もし話せたら教えてもらえるかな？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me, if you feel comfortable sharing?

dialogue.content: 友達んちはお父さんと仲いいなぁって感じるし門限とかないしうらやましい、うちは門限とかあるし、携帯とか何分話したとか数えられてるし
dialogue.English: I feel like my friends get along well with their dads, and they don't have curfews. I'm so jealous. At my house, I have a curfew, and he even counts how many minutes I've been on my phone.

dialogue.content: なるほどなるほど門限の有無もそうだし、携帯のこととかも気にしてくるんですね
dialogue.English: I see, I see. So it's not just the curfew, but he also keeps tabs on your phone usage.

dialogue.content: うん
dialogue.English: Yeah.

dialogue.content: うざくないですか？
dialogue.English: Isn't that annoying?

dialogue.content: ほっといてほしい
dialogue.English: I just want him to leave me alone.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね、それは監視されてるって思ってしまうと思う。そしてお友達のお父さんがそうではないと、うちだけなのかな？とか変わってるのかな？って
dialogue.English: I see. That would definitely make you feel like you're being watched. And when your friends' fathers aren't like that, you might wonder, "Is it just my family?" or "Is something strange about us?"

dialogue.content: 感じてしまうんですよね。
dialogue.English: You end up feeling that way, don't you?

dialogue.content: そんな感じです
dialogue.English: Yeah, something like that.

dialogue.content: ちなみにあなたにはご兄弟はいますか？
dialogue.English: By the way, do you have any siblings?

dialogue.content: 弟がいます
dialogue.English: I have a younger brother.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、弟さんにはどうですか？
dialogue.English: I see. How is he with your brother?

dialogue.content: ちょっと違うかも、ただ、弟はまだ中学生だしそんなに反抗もしないしまじめだからあんまり言われないかな。弟はおとなしいタイプだから、でも、嫌だなって感じている部分もあるんじゃないかなぁ
dialogue.English: It might be a little different. He's still in middle school, he doesn't really talk back, and he's serious, so he doesn't get told off much. He's the quiet type, but I bet there are things he dislikes too.

dialogue.content: そっかそっかではお父さんは弟さんよりもあなたにきつく言ってくるように思われているんですよね
dialogue.English: I see. So you feel that your father is stricter with you than with your brother.

dialogue.content: それは余計に、なんで私ばっかり？とかイライラしてしまうんじゃないかと感じたのだけれどそれについてはどう思いますか？
dialogue.English: I imagine that might make you feel even more irritated, thinking, "Why always me?" How do you feel about that?

dialogue.content: う～ん、私は弟と違って女だし、
dialogue.English: Hmm, unlike my brother, I'm a girl, and...

dialogue.content: うん、うん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 弟は頭もいいし要領がいいから親もかわいいと思う
dialogue.English: My brother is smart and knows how to handle things, so I think my parents find him endearing.

dialogue.content: それに比べて私は反抗的だし言いたいこと言いまくるしかわいくないから余計言われるのかも
dialogue.English: Compared to him, I'm rebellious and say what I think, not very "cute," so maybe that's why they come down on me more.

dialogue.content: そうなんだねあなたはそんな風に感じているんですね
dialogue.English: I see. So that's how you feel about it.

dialogue.content: でも自分の意見を言えることも、とっても大切だと私は思いますよ
dialogue.English: But I think being able to speak your mind is a very important thing.

dialogue.content: あなたは自分の考えをしっかり持っているんじゃないかなって感じました
dialogue.English: I get the sense that you have strong opinions of your own.

dialogue.content: 先ほど、お父さんが怒鳴ることもあるって言っていたけれどどんなふうに怒鳴るのかな？
dialogue.English: You mentioned earlier that your father sometimes yells. What is he like when he yells?

dialogue.content: 考えをしっかり持ってるって言ってもらえてうれしいです
dialogue.English: I'm happy to hear you say I have strong opinions.

dialogue.content: 親はあんまりほめてくれないから
dialogue.English: My parents don't really praise me much.

dialogue.content: お父さんはいつも怒鳴ります
dialogue.English: My dad is always yelling.

dialogue.content: うんうん、本当に大事なことだから誇りに思っていいと思うよ
dialogue.English: Yes, it's a really important quality, so I think you can be proud of it.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます、そういってもらえて本当にうれしい
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'm really happy to hear that.

dialogue.content: お父さんは話し合いとかできない人なんです
dialogue.English: My dad is not the kind of person you can have a discussion with.

dialogue.content: 感情がすぐ爆発するっていうか
dialogue.English: It's like his emotions just explode.

dialogue.content: だから家にいると息苦しい
dialogue.English: That's why it feels suffocating to be at home.

dialogue.content: そっか、そうなんだね、親御さんに褒めてもらえないってそれはつらい気持ちにもなるよね
dialogue.English: I see. Not being praised by your parents must be painful.

dialogue.content: 居場所がないって思えたり、それは息苦しくもなるよね
dialogue.English: It can make you feel like you don't have a place, and that would certainly be suffocating.

dialogue.content: うん、たぶん私が出来ないからいけないんだと思う、だからほめられないんだと思う
dialogue.English: Yeah, I guess it's because I'm not good enough. That's probably why I don't get praised.

dialogue.content: 褒めてくれないって言っていたけれどどんな時にそう思ったんですか？言える範囲でいいから聞かせてほしいな
dialogue.English: You said they don't praise you. When do you feel that way? I'd like to hear about it, if you're comfortable sharing.

dialogue.content: でも、弟はすごく頭がよくって偏差値も高くて、私は馬鹿だからいつも怒られる
dialogue.English: Well, my brother is really smart with high test scores, and I'm stupid, so I always get scolded.

dialogue.content: そうかそうか、ではもしかしたら弟さんと比べられたりすることもあるのかな？
dialogue.English: I see. So maybe you are sometimes compared to your brother?

dialogue.content: 比べたりはしないかな、私がそう思うだけ、弟は昔から頭が良くて、同じ兄弟とは思えないくらい成績が違うの、私は頑張っても全然成績が上がらない
dialogue.English: They don't really compare us, I think it's just me. My brother has always been smart, and our grades are so different you wouldn't think we're siblings. No matter how hard I try, my grades just don't improve.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね、あなたはそんな風に思うんだね。お父さんが比べてきたりするっていうよりはあなた自身がそう感じているんだね
dialogue.English: I see, that's how you feel. So it's not so much your father comparing you, but more how you yourself feel.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そんな気持ちをここで私に話してくれて私はうれしいし少しでもあなたの気持ちが和らいだらいいなと思っています
dialogue.English: I'm glad you shared those feelings with me here, and I hope that your feelings can be eased, even just a little.

dialogue.content: ありがとう、さっきは嬉しかった
dialogue.English: Thank you. What you said earlier made me happy.

dialogue.content: なんか、気持ちがふわっとなった
dialogue.English: I feel a bit lighter somehow.

dialogue.content: うんうん私もあなたがそう感じてくれてよかった色々な事悩んでしまうくらい、あなたは感受性が豊かなんだよね
dialogue.English: Mm-hm, I'm glad you feel that way. The fact that you worry about so many things just shows how sensitive you are.

dialogue.content: とにかくお父さんが本当に嫌で、この前夢でお父さんの事刺し殺す夢見ちゃった
dialogue.English: Anyway, I really hate my dad, and the other day I had a dream where I stabbed him to death.

dialogue.content: そんな夢見るってやばくないですか？
dialogue.English: Isn't it messed up to have a dream like that?

dialogue.content: そうなんだね、その夢を見たときは実際になにかお父さんとトラブルが起こったの？
dialogue.English: I see. When you had that dream, had something actually happened with your father?

dialogue.content: 夢だと無意識だしそういう過激なものが出てくることもあるよね
dialogue.English: In dreams, our unconscious mind can sometimes bring up extreme things like that.

dialogue.content: あんまり覚えてないけど、、、ずーーーーっと何年も感じていたものがそうなったのかなぁって思った。
dialogue.English: I don't remember much, but... I thought maybe it was something I'd been feeling for years and years that took that form.

dialogue.content: なんか、さすがにやばいなって思って
dialogue.English: It made me think, okay, this is really not good.

dialogue.content: 大丈夫なのかなぁ私
dialogue.English: I wonder if I'm okay.

dialogue.content: そっか何年もそう感じているのは、しんどいね頑張っているよね
dialogue.English: I see. Feeling that way for years is exhausting. You've been hanging in there.

dialogue.content: お父さんにはそういう話したことある？いやだって思っている事とか、うざいとか
dialogue.English: Have you ever talked to your father about that? About how you dislike things, or how you find him annoying?

dialogue.content: はい、ずーーーーっとしんどく思ってる。お父さんが出張だと本当にうれしい
dialogue.English: Yes, it's been hard for a very, very long time. I'm so happy when my dad is away on a business trip.

dialogue.content: そんなこと言ったら殴られます
dialogue.English: If I said something like that, I'd get hit.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね少しでも離れられると安心するよね
dialogue.English: I see. It must be a relief to have some distance from him, even for a little while.

dialogue.content: 殴ることもあるんだねどんなふうに？
dialogue.English: So he hits you sometimes. In what way?

dialogue.content: 自分の意見を聞けないとぶん殴ってきます
dialogue.English: If he can't accept my opinion, he'll hit me.

dialogue.content: びんたとか、ゲンコツとか
dialogue.English: Like slapping or punching with his knuckles.

dialogue.content: それは、いくら家族だからって本当にしてはいけないことだし
dialogue.English: That's something that should never happen, no matter if you're family.

dialogue.content: すごい怖い顔して震えながら怒ってる
dialogue.English: He gets a really scary face and shakes with anger.

dialogue.content: 犯罪になるようなことだと思うのだけれどあなたはどう思う？
dialogue.English: I believe that's something that could be considered a crime. What do you think?

dialogue.content: でも、私は怖いけど泣きながら言いたいこと言ってます　笑
dialogue.English: But, even though I'm scared, I still say what I want to say while crying. lol

dialogue.content: むかしっからそうだからそういうものかなって思ってるけど
dialogue.English: It's been like that since I was little, so I kind of thought that's just how it is.

dialogue.content: 相談員さんは親に殴られたことない？
dialogue.English: Have you ever been hit by your parents, counselor?

dialogue.content: そっかそっかそれは本当にこわいよね泣いてしまうよね
dialogue.English: I see, that must be truly frightening. It's natural to cry.

dialogue.content: 私もお父さんに頭叩かれたり、怒鳴られたり、あった
dialogue.English: I've also been smacked on the head by my father and yelled at.

dialogue.content: そっか、相談員さんもあったんだね
dialogue.English: Oh, so it happened to you too.

dialogue.content: なんか安心
dialogue.English: That's somehow reassuring.

dialogue.content: あなたは他の人に相談出来たりしている？
dialogue.English: Are you able to talk to anyone else about this?

dialogue.content: お母さんとお父さんと悪口言ってる
dialogue.English: My mom and I complain about my dad together.

dialogue.content: 笑
dialogue.English: lol

dialogue.content: うん、だからあなたが少しでも楽になれたら、って思います。
dialogue.English: Yes, so I hope you can feel even a little bit better.

dialogue.content: お母さんは私の味方してくれるから
dialogue.English: My mom is on my side.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね！じゃあお母さんとはそういう話が出来ているんだ
dialogue.English: I see! So you're able to talk with your mother about these things.

dialogue.content: うん、相談員さんもそうなんだぁって思ったらなんか気が楽になりました
dialogue.English: Yeah. Knowing you've been through something similar made me feel more at ease.

dialogue.content: うん、お母さんもお父さんから何度も泣かされているからね
dialogue.English: Yeah, my dad has made my mom cry many times, too.

dialogue.content: うちが崩壊しないのはお母さんのおかげかもしれない
dialogue.English: Maybe the reason our family hasn't fallen apart is thanks to my mom.

dialogue.content: うんうんお母さんにもつらくあたるんだね。それは見ているのも嫌だよねお母さんも耐えているんだよね
dialogue.English: Yes, so he's hard on your mother, too. It must be difficult to watch that. Your mother is enduring it as well.

dialogue.content: うん、そうかも、お母さんもかわいそう
dialogue.English: Yeah, maybe so. I feel sorry for my mom too.

dialogue.content: だからお父さんの事もっと嫌いになる
dialogue.English: That makes me hate my dad even more.

dialogue.content: 自然とそうなるよ、何も不思議なことじゃないちょっと今までお話聞いてきて、もしよかったらあなたでもお母さんでも大丈夫なんだけれど
dialogue.English: That's a natural reaction; it's not strange at all. Now, based on what I've heard so far, if you're open to it, this could be for either you or your mother, but...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes?

dialogue.content: 家庭のことで悩まれている方の専門の窓口があってねそこも安心してお話しできる場所だし柔軟に対応できるところなんだけれど
dialogue.English: There are specialized support services for people dealing with family issues. It's a safe place to talk, and they are very flexible in how they can help.

dialogue.content: そうなんだ
dialogue.English: Oh, I see.

dialogue.content: そんなところがあるんですね
dialogue.English: I didn't know a place like that existed.

dialogue.content: もし気持ちがそこに向くようならそこで相談してもいいかもしれないと思ってね
dialogue.English: If you feel up to it, I think it might help to talk to them.

dialogue.content: そんなところがあるならばちょっと興味があるからお母さんに話してみる
dialogue.English: If a place like that exists, I'm a little interested, so I'll talk to my mom about it.

dialogue.content: いきなりそこじゃなくてもまずはお母さんにそういう窓口があることを伝えてみてもいいかなって
dialogue.English: You don't have to go there right away, but maybe you could start by just telling your mother that such a service exists.

dialogue.content: そこでどんな事してくれるのかなぁ
dialogue.English: I wonder what they do there.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm.

dialogue.content: まずはお話を聞いてくれて状況を確認してくれたりお父さんにこういう事を話すと、なにされるかわからないとかあると思うから
dialogue.English: Well, first, they will listen to you and assess the situation. I imagine you might be afraid of what your father would do if you talk about these things.

dialogue.content: あなたとかお母さんの気持ちのケアをしてくれたりするよ
dialogue.English: They can provide emotional support for you and your mother.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、じゃあお母さんに話してみます。もしかしたら、お父さんビビるかもね笑
dialogue.English: I see. Then I'll talk to my mom. Maybe it'll even scare my dad a little, lol.

dialogue.content: 抱え込んでしまうことは良くないから第三者に話せるっていうところも、気持ちが安らぐ場所としてあるのもいいと思うよ
dialogue.English: It's not good to keep it all bottled up, so I think it's good to have a place where you can talk to a third party and feel at ease.

dialogue.content: そうだね笑でも本当にまたここにきてもいいし
dialogue.English: That's true, haha. But really, you're always welcome to come back here, too.

dialogue.content: いつでも待ってるから
dialogue.English: I'll always be here for you.

dialogue.content: そうなんだね、こういう事って普通にあることなんだと思って我慢していたけど
dialogue.English: I see. I thought this kind of thing was normal, so I was just enduring it.

dialogue.content: 話したら何か変わることもあることがあるって今日分かったから、そうだんしてみます。
dialogue.English: But today I realized that talking about it can sometimes change things, so I'll try reaching out.

dialogue.content: うんうん前向きに考えてくれて、色々聞かせてくれてありがとう我慢してあなたがつらくなることが少しでも減ったらいいと、本当に思う
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you for considering it positively and for sharing so much with me. I truly hope that you won't have to endure so much pain anymore.

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとう！相談員さんの事もたくさん聞いてみたいからまた来ちゃうかも笑
dialogue.English: Okay, thank you! I want to ask you a lot about yourself too, so I might be back, lol.

dialogue.content: そうね今度は私が聞いてもらうことになってしまうかもね！笑
dialogue.English: You're right, maybe next time you'll be the one listening to me! Haha.

dialogue.content: また安心していつでも来てね
dialogue.English: Please feel free to come back anytime.

dialogue.content: 同じ思いをしてきたんだって聞けただけでなんか救われた、相談員さんも今度はたくさん話してね
dialogue.English: Just hearing that you've been through something similar makes me feel saved somehow. Next time, you should share more too.

dialogue.content: うん、また来るね
dialogue.English: Yeah, I'll come again.

dialogue.content: どうもありがとう
dialogue.English: Thank you so much.

dialogue.content: うん、こちらこそありがとう！では時間になってしまったのでここで失礼するね
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you too! It looks like our time is up, so we'll have to end here for today.

dialogue.content: またね～
dialogue.English: See you~

dialogue.content: 寒いのであたたかくしてねでは、またね
dialogue.English: It's cold, so stay warm. See you again.

dialogue.content: （ロープレありがとうございました、またよろしくお願いいたします。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for the role-play. I look forward to working with you again.)

dialogue.content: (ありがとうございました、参考になりました)
dialogue.English: (Thank you, this was very helpful.)
